findings.how_to_check: Run `Select-String -Path replication/run_machineA.do -Pattern score_fs_links`; it returns no match. Running `replication/Run-MachineA.ps1` will not generate `MATCHING/results/fs_linkage_abe.tex`. Compare the inputs at lines 32-41 of `MATCHING/score_fs_links.do` with `replication/run_machineA.do`'s preflight list.
findings.suggested_fix: Add the FamilySearch link files and intermediate dependencies to `replication/run_machineA.do`'s preflight block, add `score_fs_links` to `scripts` in `run_machineA.do`, and make the configuration bootstrap in `score_fs_links.do` locate `replication/config.do` relatively or via environment variables rather than hardcoding the `D:` drive path.
findings.title: New FamilySearch scorer is omitted from the machine-A replication pipeline and preflight checks
findings.what_the_code_does: The script reads five link datasets, two divided-file directories, congruence data, and the MLP reference, writing `MATCHING/results/fs_linkage_abe.tex`. However, `replication/run_machineA.do` does not include these inputs in its preflight check, omits `score_fs_links` from `scripts`, and `score_fs_links.do:30` hardcodes `do "D:/repos/fixing_transcription_errors/replication/config.do"` if `$REP_REPO` is unset.
findings.why_it_matters: Executing the documented replication runner (`Run-MachineA.ps1`) cannot reproduce `MATCHING/results/fs_linkage_abe.tex`. Corrupted or missing FamilySearch inputs bypass preflight validation, and running the script on another machine or path fails at the hardcoded bootstrap.

findings.how_to_check: Document the provenance of `unique_ID_to_census_crosswalk1930.dta` and `unique_ID_to_census_crosswalk1940.dta`, specifically whether FamilySearch census transcriptions guided profile attachment. Compare FamilySearch and Ancestry link accuracy against an independent, hand-adjudicated census sample.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify in table notes and manuscript text that `Verified Correct` and `Recall` represent agreement with the FamilySearch-derived profile reference rather than independent ground truth. Report sensitivity or benchmark comparisons on an independent validation sample.
findings.title: Scoring FamilySearch transcriptions against FamilySearch-derived profile links introduces common-source confounding
findings.what_the_code_does: The scorer treats `mlp_training1930_1940.dta` as ground truth (`true_links`), defining `ver_*` by `histid1930 == true_histid1930` and reporting `Verified Correct` and `Recall`. Upstream in `CODE/create_linked_sample_for_MLP_training.do`, that reference is built by merging 1930 and 1940 FamilySearch tree crosswalks on `unique_ID`.
findings.why_it_matters: If FamilySearch census transcriptions, indexing conventions, or search suggestions guided profile-to-census attachments on FamilySearch, the FamilySearch-name columns and the validation reference share common errors and selection, artificially inflating FamilySearch verification and recall relative to independent transcriptions.

findings.how_to_check: Tabulate `fs_frst_used` and `fs_last_used` over the full eligible 1940 male population before matching, and compare match and verification rates across pure FamilySearch pairs, single-field hybrid pairs, and pure Ancestry fallback pairs.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify in table notes that the FamilySearch columns reflect an Ancestry-fallback policy. Retain separate first- and last-name indicators, report pre-link coverage over the population denominator, and include a balanced sensitivity check restricted to records with FamilySearch transcriptions in both fields across both censuses.
findings.title: FamilySearch columns mix selective field-level Ancestry fallback with post-linkage coverage metrics
findings.what_the_code_does: Upstream code substitutes FamilySearch names only when non-empty (`replace f_name = fs_namefrst_cleaned if fs_frst_used`, `replace l_name = fs_namelast_cleaned if fs_last_used`), falling back to Ancestry field by field. Upstream link aggregation collapses these into `fs_used = fs_frst_used | fs_last_used`. The scorer computes coverage as `count if fs_used == 1 / _N` only among successfully linked pairs, reporting it under headers labeled `FS 1930 & 1940`, `FS 1930`, and `FS 1940`.
findings.why_it_matters: The reported columns evaluate a selective hybrid fallback policy rather than pure FamilySearch transcriptions. Measuring coverage among linked pairs conditions on an outcome of the linkage process, obscuring population availability and conflating transcription quality with the selective characteristics of fallback records.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied, so claims-vs-code review was limited to comments and table labels emitted by the code; manuscript text, abstract claims, and text tables could not be verified.

The Stata pipeline was not executed end-to-end; data files on external storage (D:/SNU ECON Dropbox and F:) were inspected via read-only tools where accessible, but Stata runtime output was inferred from static source analysis.
The output LaTeX file MATCHING/results/fs_linkage_abe.tex was not compiled or rendered to PDF, so final visual formatting could not be inspected.

The exact indexing and search algorithms used by FamilySearch users and hint engines when attaching census records to FamilyTree profiles cannot be established from repository source code, so the common-source risk is classified as likely rather than verified.
Review was scoped to the uncommitted working-tree changes against HEAD.
structured_output.summary: The new FamilySearch linkage scoring script correctly handles missing ages, excludes empty strings from middle-initial agreement, accurately labels its 8+ age universe, and includes a comprehensive fail-closed replication gate checking all displayed counts and rates. However, the script is omitted from the machine-A replication runner and preflight checks, and evaluating FamilySearch links against a FamilySearch-derived profile reference introduces potential common-source bias. The single most important fix is to register the scorer and its input datasets in replication/run_machineA.do while documenting the reference's derivation in the table notes.

verified_clean.evidence: At MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:98, the denominator filter explicitly specifies `keep if age >= 8 & !missing(age)`, preventing missing age values (`.`) from exceeding 8 and inflating the denominator.
verified_clean.item: Missing ages cannot enter the denominator through Stata's missing-value ordering.

verified_clean.evidence: At MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:236-240, `keep if mi1930 != ""` & `mi1940 != ""` is enforced prior to `count if mi1930 == mi1940`, ensuring empty strings do not count as agreement.
verified_clean.item: Blank middle initials are excluded before middle-initial agreement is evaluated.

verified_clean.evidence: Target values are declared at MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:46-84; counts are checked at lines 248-254 and 349-356; percentages (`rate`, `mi`, `recall`) are verified against rounded published figures at lines 255-263; and any discrepancy sets `bad = 1` and triggers `exit 9` before table output at lines 359-362.
verified_clean.item: The fail-closed replication gate checks all printed counts, match rates, MI rates, and recall before writing the LaTeX table.

verified_clean.evidence: At MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:380, the LaTeX table heading is written as `\multicolumn{6}{l}{\textit{Men aged 8+ in the 1940 census}}`, matching the age filter at line 98.
verified_clean.item: The table panel heading accurately reflects the age-restricted male universe.

verified_clean.evidence: At MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:211-218, merges on `histid1940` and `histid1930` partition links into `unv` (neither individual in truth), `ver` (1940 individual's true partner equals candidate 1930 partner), and `con` (either 1940 individual has a different true partner or 1930 individual is linked to someone else in truth), with no overlapping or unassigned categories.
verified_clean.item: Truth classification checks both individuals and exhaustively partitions proposed links into verified, unverifiable, and contradicted.

verified_clean.evidence: At MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:297-301, pairs with `histid1940_old != histid1940_new` are classified as `status == "changed"`, and lines 331-340 and 385-387 export total changed partners as well as new/old verified partner counts in dedicated table rows.
verified_clean.item: Partner changes between linkage methods are tracked separately rather than distorting net added and net removed counts.

verified_clean.evidence: Pairs are deduplicated at MATCHING/score_fs_links.do:135, 156, and 173 (`duplicates drop histid1930 histid1940, force`), and 1930 records are deduplicated prior to Panel B comparison at lines 276 and 290.
verified_clean.item: All candidate and truth link pairs are deduplicated, preventing multi-record inflation.

verified_clean.evidence: `git status --short` confirms that MATCHING/score_fs_links.do is the only code modification; all other untracked files are review artifacts located in review/reports/.
verified_clean.item: Untracked report artifacts contain no modified code outside the target script.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
